newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's economy grew 4.8 pct last year - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's economy grew 4.8 pct last year - cenbank.

text.p: Kenya on Tuesday posted its gross domestic product (GDP) growth at 4.8 percent in 1996, lower than the forecast 6.0 percent and 4.9 percent in 1995.

The Central Bank of Kenya, in a report issued in Nairobi, also forecast economic growth at 6.0 percent in 1997 and 7.0 percent in 1998. The finance ministry has previously forecast 1997 growth at 7.0 percent and 1998 growth at 8.0 percent.

At a news briefing, Central Bank Governor Micah Cheserem hinted that because of a drought that President Daniel arap Moi has already declared a national disaster, the GDP growth estimate for 1997 was unlikely to be met.
"People have already started talking about GDP growth of just 4-5 percent," Cheserem told reporters.

Cheserem added that despite the lower-than-expected GDP growth, the economy was healthy and GDP growth was picking up from comparative depressing figures such as 0.2 percent in 1993 and 0.5 percent in 1992.
"If our objective had been to run down the economy in the first half of this decade, which it was not, then we had succeeded by 1993," the central bank said in a report.
Cheserem said real interest rates were still very high but the central bank was determined to reduce them through a combination of monetary and fiscal policies.
Interest rates on the 91-day main category of government treasury bills is now around 21 percent. Base lending rates in commercial banks ranges from 24 percent to up to 35 percent.
